Diagnosis:
The test `testEncoder()` fails because the instance method `Base64.encode(byte[])` appends a CRLF (carriage return and line feed) to its encoded output, chunking the result into multiple 76-character lines with CRLF separators. This behavior differs from the previous version Commons-Codec-1.3, which did not chunk lines or append CRLF by default when using the instance method `encode()`.

Inspecting the implementation of `Base64.encode(byte[])` reveals it calls a private method `getEncodeLength()` which calculates the allocation size for the output buffer. This length calculation includes extra space for line separators (CRLF sequences) if chunking is enabled. The constructor `Base64()` in the current version apparently sets a default line length that triggers chunking.

The `encode(byte[] pArray, int i, int length)` method encodes the input data in blocks, and when the line length limit is reached, it inserts the configured line separator (`lineSeparator`) (in this case a CRLF) into the output buffer. This confirms the chunking behavior on encoding.

From the constructors shown, the default `Base64()` constructor calls `this(false)`, which calls another constructor that sets a default `lineLength` and `lineSeparator` (likely 76 and CRLF). That results in chunking and appending of CRLF even on the default instance `encode()` method.

The static method `Base64.encodeBase64()` does not suffer from this because it likely uses different or no chunking parameters, matching behavior from the previous version.

Thus the root cause is that the default instance `Base64` encoder now has chunking enabled with a default 76-character line length and CRLF line separator, causing the output of `encode()` to differ from the previous version and produce additional trailing CRLFs and segmented lines, causing the test to fail when it expects continuous base64 encoding without inserted CRLFs.

This behavior was introduced in version 1.4 according to the bug report, but was not present in 1.3. Users needing the old behavior must explicitly disable chunking by creating `Base64` instances with line-length 0 or null lineSeparator.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this base64 chunking and CRLF appending issue.

In summary: The failing test expects a single continuous base64 output, but the instance `Base64.encode()` now chunks into 76-char lines ended by CRLF, causing the assertion to fail.

Propose fixing the instance encoder's default constructor or encode method to allow disabling of chunking or to match the previous no-chunking behavior by default. Possibly add a no-chunking constructor or fix the default lineLength/lineSeparator settings.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
